title: Value Cards Trading
short_description: Choose and exchange value cards, finding the values that best resonate with you.
premise: Participants begin with different value cards, trade to assemble a hand they can stand behind, and then account for what they kept, what they let go, and which values proved difficult to compare.
group_size: Three people per table; any number of tables
preview_label: A shared table with value cards arranged between private hands and a trading area
overview: The Value Cards are a deck of 36 cards, each naming one value, such as Community, Honesty or Courage, with a short definition and a picture. The deck is printed in two groups of 18, framed in crimson or navy, and each card carries the icon of the category its value belongs to in Shalom Schwartz’s theory of basic human values. In Value Cards Trading, three players share the 18 cards of the base deck, dealt 6 each and laid face up on the table, so everyone can see what everyone holds. They trade, the same number of cards in each direction, to build the hand that best reflects the values they care about most, and each player trades at least once with each of the other two. When trading ends, each player picks the top three values in their final hand. Sharing those choices, within the trio or beyond it, is optional. A debrief follows.

title: Leadership and Knowledge in Popular Rule
short_description: Make a collective decision while information, authority, and the costs of delay are unevenly distributed.
premise: A group must act on a shared problem, but no participant begins with the whole picture. The table makes competing proposals and unequal knowledge visible, then asks the group to examine how it reached a decision.
group_size: 9–20 people per city, several cities at once
preview_label: A shared decision table with evidence, proposals, and a decision area
